Spring vs Spring Boot?

Spring | Spring Boot
Lots of manual configuration (XML or Java) | Auto-configuration with sensible defaults
Deploy a WAR to an external server | Embedded Tomcat/Jetty/Undertow, executable fat JAR
Manage dependency versions yourself | Starters plus a managed BOM
No production tooling | Actuator: health, metrics
Boot is Spring. It just removes the boilerplate.
How does auto-configuration work?

@EnableAutoConfiguration loads the candidate classes listed in META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports (it was spring.factories before Boot 2.7). Each one is guarded by @Conditional* annotations. For example, DataSourceAutoConfiguration only runs if a JDBC driver is on the classpath and you haven't defined your own DataSource. Your beans always take priority. To exclude one: @SpringBootApplication(exclude = DataSourceAutoConfiguration.class).
What are starters? Name a few.

Starters are dependency descriptors that bundle compatible libraries. Examples: spring-boot-starter-web (MVC, Tomcat, Jackson), -data-jpa (Hibernate, HikariCP), -security, -validation, -actuator, -test (JUnit 5, Mockito, AssertJ), -webflux, -cache, -amqp, and spring-kafka added directly (there is no Kafka starter before Boot 4).
@Value vs @ConfigurationProperties?

@Value("${app.x:default}") injects a single value and supports SpEL. @ConfigurationProperties binds a whole group of properties into a type-safe object. It supports relaxed binding, validation (@Validated) and IDE metadata. Use it for anything more than one or two values.
Property source precedence order?

From highest to lowest (simplified): command-line args → SPRING_APPLICATION_JSON → Java system properties → OS environment variables → application-{profile}.yml → application.yml → @PropertySource → defaults. Files outside the jar override the ones packaged inside it.
What is Spring Boot Actuator?

Production-ready endpoints under /actuator: health (with liveness and readiness probes for Kubernetes), info, metrics, prometheus, env, beans, mappings, loggers (change log levels at runtime), threaddump, heapdump. It uses Micrometer for metrics. Secure the sensitive endpoints.
How to change embedded server / port? How to deploy as WAR?

Port: server.port=9090 (use 0 for a random port). Server: exclude spring-boot-starter-tomcat and add -jetty or -undertow. WAR: set <packaging>war</packaging>, mark Tomcat as provided, and extend SpringBootServletInitializer.
CommandLineRunner vs ApplicationRunner?

Both run once after the context has started (seeding data, warm-up). CommandLineRunner.run(String... args) receives the raw args. ApplicationRunner.run(ApplicationArguments) receives parsed options. Control the order with @Order.

What changed in Spring Boot 3?

Requires Java 17+ and Spring Framework 6. Moved from javax → jakarta packages. GraalVM native image support (AOT). Observability with Micrometer Tracing (Sleuth was removed). ProblemDetail errors. HTTP interface clients (@HttpExchange). Virtual thread support (spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true, Boot 3.2). RestClient (3.2).
What does spring-boot-devtools do?
Automatic restart when classpath files change, LiveReload, and dev-friendly defaults such as disabled template caching. It's turned off automatically in a packaged jar running in production.
How to create a custom starter / auto-configuration?

Write a @AutoConfiguration class with @ConditionalOnClass and @ConditionalOnMissingBean beans and a @ConfigurationProperties class, and register it in META-INF/spring/…AutoConfiguration.imports. Package it as xyz-spring-boot-starter.
RestTemplate vs WebClient vs RestClient vs Feign?

RestTemplate: synchronous, in maintenance mode. WebClient: reactive and non-blocking (WebFlux). RestClient (Boot 3.2): a modern synchronous fluent API, the replacement for RestTemplate. OpenFeign: declarative interface clients, popular in microservices. There's also Spring's own @HttpExchange interfaces.
How do you enable caching / scheduling / async?

@EnableCaching + @Cacheable("users"), @CacheEvict, @CachePut (with Caffeine or Redis). @EnableScheduling + @Scheduled(cron = "0 0 * * * *") or fixedRate. @EnableAsync + @Async returning CompletableFuture. All three are proxy-based, so self-invocation doesn't work.
What exactly does @SpringBootApplication do, and why should it sit in a root package?

It combines @SpringBootConfiguration, @EnableAutoConfiguration and @ComponentScan. Scanning and @AutoConfigurationPackage start from its package. Put it in a sub-package and sibling packages are not scanned, and JPA entities or repositories there are not found. You can move it with scanBasePackages, @EntityScan and @EnableJpaRepositories, but the root package is simpler.
Why are user beans able to override auto-configured beans?

Two facts combine. AutoConfigurationImportSelector is a DeferredImportSelector, so its classes are processed after all user configuration. And auto-configured beans carry @ConditionalOnMissingBean. So when the condition is evaluated, your bean is already registered, and the auto-configured one is skipped.
I added a DataSource dependency and the app fails with "Failed to configure a DataSource". Why? What are the options?

A starter brought JDBC classes onto the class path, so DataSourceAutoConfiguration activated, but no URL is configured, and no embedded database is available. Supply spring.datasource.url, add H2, or exclude it: @SpringBootApplication(exclude = DataSourceAutoConfiguration.class). The message comes from a FailureAnalyzer, which produces those readable startup errors.
How do you find out why a bean was not created?

Run with --debug and read the conditions report, or use /actuator/conditions. Each auto-configuration shows which condition failed: for example, "@ConditionalOnClass did not find required class". If your own component is missing, check the scan package, the @Profile, and any @Conditional.
What is the difference between spring.factories and AutoConfiguration.imports today?

Auto-configurations are listed only in the .imports file since Boot 3.0. spring.factories is still used for other extension points: ApplicationListener, EnvironmentPostProcessor, ApplicationContextInitializer, FailureAnalyzer. A library upgraded from Boot 2 with auto-configuration in spring.factories silently does nothing on Boot 3.
Describe the Spring Boot startup sequence.

The constructor deduces the application type and loads initializers and listeners. run() prepares the Environment, reading config files. It creates the context, applies initializers, and loads sources. refresh() processes configuration including auto-configuration, creates the web server in onRefresh, creates singletons, and starts accepting. Then ApplicationStartedEvent, runners, and ApplicationReadyEvent. Any failure triggers ApplicationFailedEvent, and failure analyzers print advice.
Output: precedence. application.yml has server.port=8080, env var SERVER_PORT=8081, JVM -Dserver.port=8082, and argument --server.port=8083. Which wins? Remove the argument?

8083: command-line arguments are higher. Without it, 8082: Java system properties beat OS environment variables. Without that, 8081, then 8080. Many answers put environment variables above system properties; the documented order is the reverse.
A value in application-prod.yml is ignored in production even though prod is active. Why?

Something of higher precedence defines it: an environment variable set by a chart, a system property, or an external config file, such as config/application.yml in the working directory, which outranks a packaged profile file. Check /actuator/env, which lists every source containing the key and which one wins. Also check for a typo in the profile activation.
Can you use YAML with @PropertySource?

Not directly: it supports .properties and XML. YAML needs a custom PropertySourceFactory. In Boot, the normal route is spring.config.import, which takes YAML and also participates correctly in precedence.
How do you bind a complex list or map from YAML, and override it with an environment variable?

app:
  hosts: [a.internal, b.internal]
  limits: { gold: 100, silver: 10 }
Use List<String> hosts and Map<String, Integer> limits in a properties record. Environment form: APP_HOSTS_0=x, APP_LIMITS_GOLD=200. Lists are replaced as a whole by a higher source, not merged element by element. Maps merge by key. Environment variable names lose case, so map keys become lowercase.
How do you validate configuration at startup?

Add @Validated and constraints to a @ConfigurationProperties type. Startup fails with a clear report if the value is missing or invalid, which is better than failing on the first request. It needs a Bean Validation implementation on the class path. Records with @DefaultValue avoid null defaults.
How can you refresh configuration without restarting?

Plain Boot binds once at startup, so no. Spring Cloud adds @RefreshScope and a /refresh endpoint that rebuilds marked beans. On Kubernetes, the usual pattern is immutable config plus a rolling restart. Log levels are an exception: /actuator/loggers changes them live.
How do you create a multi-module starter so that it does not force dependencies on users?

Put code in an auto-configure module, with integration dependencies marked optional. Guard each integration with @ConditionalOnClass. The starter module depends on the auto-configure module plus the common libraries. Test with ApplicationContextRunner, using FilteredClassLoader to simulate a missing class. Use @ConditionalOnMissingBean so that users can override.
Does the default Tomcat handle only 200 concurrent requests? What actually limits it?

Three numbers apply. max-connections (8192): accepted sockets. threads.max (200): requests actively being processed. accept-count (100): the OS backlog once connections are full. A 201st active request waits for a thread rather than failing. Beyond connections plus backlog, clients see refused or timed-out connections. In practice the database pool usually limits you first.
Why does a Boot JAR need a special loader? What is in BOOT-INF?

The JDK's URLClassLoader cannot read a JAR within a JAR. Copying classes together ("shading") causes clashes. So Boot keeps dependencies as nested JARs in BOOT-INF/lib, classes in BOOT-INF/classes, and JarLauncher in the top level, with a loader that reads nested entries. Consequently resource.getFile() fails for class-path entries.
Why are layered images better, and how do you customize layers?

Docker reuses unchanged layers, so a typical deployment pushes only a few MB of application classes rather than the whole fat JAR, and pulls are quick. You can define custom layers in the plugin configuration, for example a separate layer for company libraries. Copy order in the Dockerfile matters: least-changing first, because a change invalidates all layers above it.
Buildpacks vs Dockerfile vs Jib?

Buildpacks give a good secure image without a Dockerfile, and rebasing can patch the OS layer without rebuilding the app. A Dockerfile is the most flexible and familiar. Jib needs no daemon, so it works in restricted CI. For a platform team standardizing many services, Buildpacks or Jib reduce drift.
Users get 502 errors during every deployment. How do you fix it?

Verify graceful shutdown is on, and that Java is PID 1 with exec-form entrypoint, so SIGTERM arrives. Add a preStop sleep for endpoint propagation. Make terminationGracePeriodSeconds exceed the shutdown timeout. Add a readiness probe so new pods get traffic only when ready. Check that the load balancer's idle timeout exceeds the app's keep-alive timeout, a common cause of 502s even outside deployments.
Where should the warm-up go: @PostConstruct, CommandLineRunner, or ApplicationReadyEvent?

In a CommandLineRunner or ApplicationRunner, if traffic must wait: readiness turns true only after runners. ApplicationReadyEvent runs after readiness, so traffic is already flowing. @PostConstruct runs too early, and on a raw object. A failed runner stops startup, so catch errors if warm-up is optional.
How do you configure ProblemDetail globally, and how do you add custom fields?

Set spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled=true for framework exceptions. For your own, throw ErrorResponseException or a subclass, or return ProblemDetail from an @ExceptionHandler, and call setProperty("key", value) for extension members, which serialize at the top level. Extend ResponseEntityExceptionHandler to customize standard errors. Titles and details can be localized through MessageSource codes.
Why do I get a 401 or empty response instead of my error JSON with Spring Security?

The error forward to /error is a separate dispatch, and Spring Security 6 applies authorization to all dispatcher types. If /error is not permitted, an anonymous client gets 401 rather than the real 400 or 500 body. Permit /error, or map errors in @RestControllerAdvice so that no forward happens.
What does spring.threads.virtual.enabled change, and what can break?

The server's request threads, applicationTaskExecutor, and scheduling use virtual threads. What can break: exhausting the connection pool or overloading a downstream, as there is no longer a thread limit acting as a throttle; pinning on Java before 24 with synchronized around I/O; heavy thread-local caches; and apps exiting early without spring.main.keep-alive. Run a load test, and watch pool wait times.
Native image vs JVM for a service. How do you decide?

Native suits scale-to-zero, serverless, and CLI tools, where startup and memory dominate. A long-running high-throughput service generally benefits from the JIT and has simpler tooling: full heap dumps, agents, and normal profilers. Consider also that builds take minutes and use much memory, and dynamic libraries may need hints. CDS or the AOT cache gives part of the startup gain at low risk.
What does AOT processing generate?

Java source that registers bean definitions without reflection, class files for proxies, and JSON reachability hints under META-INF/native-image. It freezes the outcome of conditions and profiles at build time, so these cannot change at runtime. You can also use the output on a normal JVM.
@SpringBootTest vs @WebMvcTest: when does each make sense? Why is my suite slow?

@WebMvcTest verifies HTTP mapping, validation, and serialization with mocked services. @SpringBootTest verifies real wiring end to end. Slowness normally comes from many distinct contexts: differing @MockitoBean sets, properties, profiles, and @DirtiesContext. Share a base configuration and containers to maximize context reuse.
How do you upgrade a Boot 2.7 service to Boot 3 or 4?

Clear deprecations on 2.7. Raise Java to 17 or higher. Replace javax with jakarta, using OpenRewrite. Update libraries that are not Jakarta-ready. Convert security to SecurityFilterChain. Use the properties migrator. Handle Hibernate 6 changes and URL-matching changes. Go to the latest 3.x before 4, then address Spring 7, Jackson 3 and starter changes. Rely on integration tests and canary deployment.
What breaks when moving from Jackson 2 to Jackson 3 in Boot 4?

Packages change from com.fasterxml.jackson to tools.jackson, except that annotations stay in com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation. The main type is JsonMapper, which is immutable and built through a builder. Custom serializers and modules need updating, and certain defaults differ, so response formats may change. Contract tests catch this. Boot 4 retains a route for keeping Jackson 2 during migration.
Is it a good idea to make all beans lazy?

It speeds up startup, but moves errors to the first request, makes that request slow, and hides problems that a failed start would reveal. Spring's eager default provides fail-fast behavior. For a production service, prefer it; lazy mode can make sense in development. Use @Lazy(false) to exempt specific beans.

What happens if two auto-configurations define the same bean name?

Bean overriding is off, so the second registration raises BeanDefinitionOverrideException, unless it is guarded by @ConditionalOnMissingBean. Correct auto-configurations use ordering with after and the condition. Setting spring.main.allow-bean-definition-overriding=true hides the conflict.
Design: how would you standardize 50 microservices on Boot?

Publish an internal parent or BOM that aligns versions, an internal starter for logging, tracing, security and error format, plus a project template. Enforce rules with ArchUnit or build checks, and automate upgrades with Renovate and OpenRewrite. Provide a golden image or Buildpack configuration. Avoid putting business logic in shared starters; they should hold cross-cutting concerns only, and be versioned so that services can upgrade independently.
Refreshing an Angular route such as /orders/7 shows a 404 or the Whitelabel page. Why, and how do you fix it?

The Angular router uses HTML5 URLs, so on refresh the browser asks the server for /orders/7, and no controller or file matches it. Configure a fallback that serves index.html for unknown, non-API, non-file paths, using a PathResourceResolver or a forwarding controller. Then Angular's router takes over. Keep /api/** out of the fallback, so that a wrong API URL still returns a real 404 JSON response and not HTML.
Should Angular be bundled into the Boot JAR or deployed separately?

Bundled: one artifact and one origin, so no CORS. It suits internal apps and small teams. But a UI change needs a backend release, and static files are served by the JVM. Separate (CDN or Nginx): independent deployments, edge caching, and the API scales separately. You then need CORS, or a reverse proxy that puts both under one domain. That proxy setup also keeps cookie-based auth simple. For most production systems, separate deployment behind one domain is the cleanest choice.
Uploads over 1 MB fail with MaxUploadSizeExceededException. What do you do?

Raise spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size and max-request-size to a deliberate limit, not to unlimited. Also check any proxy limit in front, such as Nginx client_max_body_size. Handle the exception in @RestControllerAdvice and return a 413 Payload Too Large ProblemDetail. Add a matching size check in Angular, so the user gets feedback before uploading. For very large files, use presigned object-storage URLs instead of streaming through the app.
What is a profile group? Can application-prod.yml activate another profile?

A group (spring.profiles.group.prod=proddb,prodmq) expands one active profile into several. A profile-specific file cannot set spring.profiles.active or include. Boot rejects this at startup, because a profile that activates other profiles made the old loading order unpredictable. Define the activation in a group in application.yml, or set it from outside with an environment variable or argument.
The API silently ignores a misspelled JSON field such as "emial". Why, and should it?

Boot's ObjectMapper turns off FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES, so unknown fields are dropped. This is the "tolerant reader" approach, which helps API evolution because older servers accept newer clients. The cost is that typos go unnoticed. Combine it with Bean Validation (@NotBlank email), so that a missing required field still fails. If you need strict input, set spring.jackson.deserialization.fail-on-unknown-properties=true. Then a typo returns 400, but every client must stop sending fields the server does not know.
I declared my own ObjectMapper bean and now dates and modules behave differently. Why?

Boot's JacksonAutoConfiguration backs off when you define an ObjectMapper bean, so its builder defaults no longer apply: the Java time module, ISO dates, the relaxed unknown-property setting, and the spring.jackson.* properties. Use a Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer (or JsonMapperBuilderCustomizer in Boot 4) or properties to tweak the mapper instead of replacing it. If you really need a second mapper, build it from the injected builder.
@ConditionalOnClass vs @ConditionalOnBean vs @ConditionalOnProperty: what does each check?

| @ConditionalOnClass | @ConditionalOnBean / OnMissingBean | @ConditionalOnProperty
Checks | A class is on the classpath | A bean of a type or name is (or is not) in the context | A property exists or has a given value
Typical use | Configure only when a library is present | Back off when the user defined their own bean | Feature switches such as app.cache.enabled=true
Order sensitive? | No | Yes: only sees beans registered so far | No
Safe in user config? | Yes | Risky: use it in auto-configuration classes | Yes
Rule of thumb: OnClass answers "is the library here?", OnMissingBean answers "has the user already decided?", OnProperty answers "did ops switch it on?". Bean conditions are reliable only in auto-configuration, which runs after user configuration.
spring-boot-starter-web vs spring-boot-starter-webflux: which do you pick, and what if both are on the classpath?

| starter-web (Spring MVC) | starter-webflux (WebFlux)
Model | Servlet API, one thread per request | Reactive streams, non-blocking event loop
Default server | Tomcat | Reactor Netty
Return types | Plain objects, ResponseEntity | Mono, Flux
Fits with | JPA/JDBC, blocking libraries | R2DBC, reactive clients, streaming
Both on classpath | Boot configures Spring MVC; WebFlux is only used for WebClient
Rule of thumb: with JPA and a normal REST API, use starter-web, and turn on virtual threads if you need more concurrency. Pick WebFlux only when the whole call chain is non-blocking. Adding webflux just to get WebClient is fine; it does not switch the app to reactive.

@Mock vs @MockBean vs @MockitoBean: what is the difference?

| @Mock | @MockBean | @MockitoBean
From | Mockito | Spring Boot | Spring Framework 6.2+
Spring context | None, plain unit test | Replaces a bean in the context | Replaces a bean in the context
Status | Current | Deprecated since Boot 3.4 | The replacement for @MockBean
Speed | Fastest | Each distinct set of mocks can create a new cached context | Same caching concern
Rule of thumb: test service logic with @Mock and @InjectMocks, no Spring. Use @MockitoBean in slice tests such as @WebMvcTest. Many different mock combinations across test classes are a common reason a suite builds too many contexts.
